newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE tries to halt pre-poll fraud in Bosnian town.
newsitem.headline: OSCE tries to halt pre-poll fraud in Bosnian town.

text.p: International supervisors in Bosnia said on Thursday they had removed several Serb election officials in an attempt to halt fraudulent registration of voters in the disputed town of Brcko.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said six election officials had been disqualified and that the registration process would be repeated in Serb-controlled Brcko for municipal polls in September.

Robert Frowick, head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, told reporters that the president and secretary of the local election commission had been removed as well as the directors of all four registration centres in Brcko.
Bosnian Serb and Moslem-Croat authorities see the municipal vote in September as a battle for territory contested during the 1992-95 war, particularly in Brcko.
The Serbs, who seized the town at the outset of the war 1992, are anxious to keep control of Brcko because it serves as the only link between Serb-held territory in western and eastern Bosnia.
Moslem-Croat federation leaders value the town's position along the river Sava and say refugees who were expelled by Serb forces have a right to return under the Dayton peace accords.

Major powers have struggled to defuse tensions surrounding Brcko since a peace treaty in 1995 left the town's future status unresolved. An international arbiter postponed a final decision until next year.
Frowick said the ruling Serb Democratic Party (SDS) in Bosnian Serb territory was implicated in the fraud and he threatened to take action if abuses continued.
"It is no secret that the SDS is the principal party and the most influential party in Republika Srpska (Serb republic) and we are encountering too many problems," Frowick said.
"If there are any further problems then we will move to the practice of removing candidates and aiming directly at the party."
Frowick declined to specify when such a decision could be made if registration problems persisted in Brcko.
The leadership of the ultra-nationalist SDS keeps tight control over the country's Serb entity and remains loyal to indicted war criminal and former Bosnian Serb president Radovan Karadzic.
The OSCE, which is overseeing the local elections, had already struck some SDS candidates off ballots in the northwest Banja Luka region three weeks ago.
OSCE supervisors in Brcko found numerous falsified identification documents, with some Serbs saying they resided in heavily damaged neighbourhoods where there were no habitable buildings.
An OSCE spokesman also said the deadline for in-country registration had been extended to June 28 from June 16. Some 1.8 million people have signed up to vote since registration began on May 6.
The OSCE has extended out-of-country registration for Bosnian refugees until June 14.
